title: Microbundle Crediting Playbook and PRD
author: Asha Patel
body:
Microbundle Crediting Playbook and PRD

Summary
-------
This document defines the Microbundle Crediting model (short: Microbundles), the product requirements for self-serve developers, the billing and reconciliation rules, and an operational playbook for rollout and rollback. Microbundles are small, attachable credit packs (fractional token/feature credits) intended to enable low-friction feature gating, inexpensive development experimentation, and per-route micropricing for high-cardinality use cases (edge agents, mobile SDKs, and partner integrations).

Goals
-----
- Enable customers to purchase and allocate small units of consumption-credit (microbundles) to routes, features, or teams.
- Support fractional consumption (credits consumed at 0.001-credit granularity) to keep costs commensurate with short-lived/low-volume workloads.
- Provide transparent metering and reconciliation with accuracy SLOs suitable for billing (monthly reconciliation) and near-real-time UX (estimate & reserve APIs).
- Offer a simple self-serve console and API for buying, gifting, and allocating microbundles.

Non-goals
---------
- Not intended to replace enterprise reserved capacity or large token bundles.
- Does not include long-term commitment discounts at launch (that is a later phase).

Definitions
-----------
- Microbundle: A purchasable pack that carries N credit units and meta-tags (feature tag, route tag, expiration).
- Credit unit: The internal currency used to pay for generation, embedding, or reranking operations. 1 credit unit is decoupled from tokens; conversion is defined per model/profile.
- Fractional credit: We charge/consume credits at 0.001 precision to support micro-usage.

Design overview
---------------
High-level: customers buy microbundles via the Console or Billing API. Microbundles are recorded on the customer account and can be: assigned to routes, gifted between subaccounts, or consumed directly by passing a bundle_id in the request header. The runtime will prefer bundle meter consumption when present, falling back to normal per-token billing when exhausted or absent.

Key constructs:
- bundle_id: UUID that maps to a bundle ledger entry.
- allocation: assignment of bundle_id to a route/team with an optional monthly cap.
- reserve_token API: short reservation token that guarantees credit for a single request (used by offline/mobile flows).

Microbundle tiers (initial public offering)
----------------------------------------
| Tier name | Credits | Typical use case | Price (USD) | Expiry |
|-----------|---------|------------------:|-----------:|--------|
| nano      | 10      | quick dogfooding / API keys for PoC | $0.49  | 90d |
| small     | 100     | small feature trial or sandbox | $3.99   | 180d |
| devbox    | 1,000   | light developer-heavy testing | $29.99  | 365d |
| team-mini | 10,000  | small team experiments | $249.00 | 365d |

Note: pricing above is list; final prices subject to regional taxes and currency rounding. Implementation will support promo codes and partner grants.

Metering rules and conversion semantics
--------------------------------------
1) Consumption path: when a request includes header X-Redwood-Bundle-ID: <bundle_id>, the serving runtime will perform these steps in order:
   a) Check allocation for route/model compatibility.
   b) Estimate credit cost using the model performance profile (credits_per_token or credits_per-inference).
   c) Attempt to reserve fractional credits from the bundle ledger atomically.
   d) If reservation succeeds, proceed and debit on completion; if it fails (insufficient), fall back to per-token charging.

2) Estimation examples (JSON):
```json
{
  "model": "rwkv-34b-quant",
  "input_tokens": 64,
  "output_tokens_estimate": 128,
  "credits_per_token": 0.0025,
  "estimated_credits": 0.48
}
```

3) Fractional rounding: We store ledger balances as integers in milli-credits (1 credit = 1000 milli-credits). All reservations and debits are in milli-credits to avoid floating point issues.

Billing & reconciliation SLOs
----------------------------
- Real-time estimate accuracy: estimate vs actual debit should be within +/-15% on median workloads (measured per model-profile) for the 30-day canary window.
- Billing accuracy (ledger correctness): 99.995% monthly accuracy for credits debited vs consumption events (target for production).
- Reconciliation latency: all debit events must be visible in billing ledger within 60 seconds of request completion.

Required telemetry (minimum)
- metric: microbundle.estimate_median_error (target < 15%)
- metric: microbundle.debit_latency_seconds.p95 (target < 2s)
- metric: microbundle.ledger_discrepancies_monthly_count (target < 5 for global accounts)
- logs: reservation.debug logs with bundle_id, route, estimate, reserved_milli_credits

Console & API UX
----------------
Console changes (high level):
- Billing -> Microbundles page: purchase flow, apply promo, view history.
- Route management: ‘assign microbundle’ modal with cap & expiry.
- Usage insights: per-bundle consumption timeline and per-route spend breakdown.

API surface (initial)
- POST /v1/microbundles/purchase {tier, quantity, promo_code?} -> 201 { bundle_ids[] }
- POST /v1/microbundles/{bundle_id}/allocate {route_id, monthly_cap_milli_credits?} -> 200
- GET /v1/microbundles/{bundle_id}/ledger -> 200 {balance_milli_credits, history[] }
- POST /v1/microbundles/estimate -> 200 {estimated_milli_credits} (public preview)

Example: reserve flow (CLI)
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/microbundles/estimate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input_tokens":32,"expected_output":64}'
```

PRD acceptance criteria (must pass to ship)
-------------------------------------------
1) End-to-end flow: purchase -> allocate -> consume -> ledger debit verified in billing within 60s.
2) Console pages ship with purchase and allocation UI (QA checklist attached).
3) Estimate accuracy median error < 15% for eight representative models (small, medium, large).
4) Service-level dashboards and alerting enabled (see telemetry).
5) Can be toggled per-customer via feature-flag (allowlist for early customers).

Rollout plan and canary metrics
-------------------------------
Phase 0: internal dogfood (2 weeks)
- Enable feature-flag for internal accounts. Target metrics: estimate_error_median < 18%, debit_latency_p95 < 2s.

Phase 1: Invite-only customers (4 weeks)
- 5–10 customers, nightly reconciliation checks.
- Measurement windows: 7-day rolling for estimate error and ledger discrepancy rate.

Phase 2: Gradual public rollout (8 weeks)
- 10% percent traffic first week, 25% second week, 50% third week, 100% final week.
- Automatic gating: if ledger_discrepancies_monthly_count > 10 or debit_latency_p95 > 5s, pause rollout and revert traffic to non-bundle charging.

Rollback & incident playbook
---------------------------
1) Detect: alert triggered (discrepancy count or debit latency).
2) Mitigate: toggle feature-flag to disable bundle acceptance at the routing tier (runtime will fallback to per-token charging).
3) Assess: run reconciliation job to enumerate affected bundle_ids and estimate exposure.
4) Communicate: incident channel #inc-billing and customer success notify affected customers within 24h.
5) Remediate: apply corrective ledger adjustments and issue credits as necessary.
6) Postmortem: 72-hour review with engineering, product, SRE, and billing.

Security and compliance considerations
------------------------------------
- Bundle metadata and ledger entries must be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed).
- Audit log: every debit, reservation, and allocation change must be retained for 13 months for billing disputes.
- RBAC: only billing admin roles and route-owners may allocate bundles.

Open questions (to resolve before GA)
------------------------------------
- International pricing and currency rounding strategy for sub-dollar microbundles.
- Legal wording for expiry and refund policy for unused microbundles.
- Interplay with enterprise reserved capacity: can we auto-fallback to reserved capacity without double-billing?

Ownership and timeline
----------------------
- Product owner: Asha Patel (product)
- Engineering lead: Diego Morales (billing infra)
- SRE / Observability: Nora Ahmed
- Estimated milestones: prototype & internal dogfood complete by 2028-07-12; invite-only by 2028-08-09; GA targeted 2028-10-01 (subject to acceptance criteria).

Appendices
---------
A) Sample ledger entry (CSV columns): bundle_id, timestamp, event_type, milli_credits_delta, resulting_balance_milli, request_id, model_profile
B) QA checklist highlights: purchase redemption test, concurrent reservation stress test (10k/s), reconciliation end-to-end test (100k events), security KMS key rotation impact test.
